chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Asheym, who said:

Al-Husayn wrote to Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! A man vowed to fast a known number of days, so he fasted some of them, then he fell ill and broke his fast. Should he begin his fasting anew, or should he count what has passed?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'He should count what has passed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a vowed fast if one breaks it due to illness before completing the days?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the principle of partial fulfillment in *nadhr* (vows), ruling that days already fasted are credited even if interrupted by illness, preventing the need to restart the count. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on ease (*taysir*) and the validity of partial performance in voluntary acts of worship, distinguishing it from obligatory fasts where makeup days are required. The ruling underscores the importance of intention and continuity in fulfilling personal religious commitments.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Ahmad Bin Asheym who said,

‘Al-Husayn wrote to (Imam) Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! A man vows that he would be Fasting for a known (number of) days. So he Fasts some of these, then he fell ill, so he broke. Should he begin his Fasting or can he count with what is past?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote to him: ‘He can count what is past’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn ‘Ushaym who has said the following:

“Al-Husayn once wrote to al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, a man had vowed to fast for certain days and fasted a few days, then he became ill and stopped fasting. Is he required to start fasting all over again or are the days that he had fasted are counted?’ He (the Imam) wrote the answer that said, ‘The days that he had fasted are also counted.’”
